claims.claim: Huawei Health Kit is a supported application integration surface for permissioned health and fitness records rather than an unrestricted personal account API.
claims.evidence: Huawei's introduction describes application access to a user's health and fitness data following authorization.

claims.claim: Huawei developer registration and identity verification are a separate prerequisite from Health Kit app setup and user authorization.
claims.evidence: Huawei's developer-account documentation describes registration and identity verification before application service configuration.

claims.claim: Health Kit access requires a configured Huawei developer application and service setup.
claims.evidence: Huawei's integration preparation guide places Health Kit behind developer project, application and signing configuration.

claims.claim: Health Kit app-level health-data permissions require an application process separate from end-user authorization.
claims.evidence: Huawei documents app-level Health Kit permission application independently from the user authorization flow.

claims.claim: A Health Kit application must obtain user authorization for the health-data permissions it requests.
claims.evidence: Huawei's authorization guide defines permission-scoped authorization rather than blanket account access.

claims.claim: Huawei's public Health Kit documentation does not establish API availability for every collected or derived value shown in Huawei Health.
claims.evidence: The development overview describes typed capability areas but publishes no complete Huawei Health screen-to-interface parity statement.

claims.claim: No public, versioned Huawei Health archive schema or completeness guarantee was located in Huawei's cited consumer privacy policy as of the evidence date.
claims.evidence: The policy provides rights and regional process context without a Huawei Health field inventory, format or retention contract.

claims.claim: Hitrava documents an in-app Huawei Health privacy workflow and project-stated support for Huawei's 2025 password-encrypted ZIP layout.
claims.evidence: The project documents Privacy Center > Request Your Data > Health, an email download, encrypted ZIP input and support for a 2025 ZIP layout; it does not guarantee arbitrary regional/current archives.

claims.claim: Hitrava converts supplied Huawei workout data to HiTrack, JSON and TCX outputs but does not retrieve a user's complete Huawei Health account.
claims.evidence: The project operates on privacy ZIP, JSON or legacy files and lists workout conversion features rather than cloud authentication or whole-account parsing.

claims.claim: Hitrava is source-available under a custom NPOSL-3.0 licence while GitHub reports its SPDX licence as NOASSERTION.
claims.evidence: The repository license file contains the custom non-profit source licence; GitHub repository metadata does not assign an SPDX identifier.

claims.claim: Huawei Health Importer contains parsers and fixtures for privacy-export heart rate, SpO2, body composition, sleep stages and daily activity records.
claims.evidence: The MIT project maps named Huawei export folders and data-point types to Apple Health; this is community-observed archive evidence, not a provider completeness guarantee.

claims.claim: Huawei Health Importer's CH100/AH100 workflow recovers model-specific body-composition history from a separate local HW100.db database rather than Huawei Health cloud export.
claims.evidence: The project documents the separate Huawei Body Fat Scale companion app, iOS backup extraction, SQLCipher database and static-key reverse engineering.

claims.claim: huawei-health-to-health-connect parses Huawei privacy-export weight and body-fat JSON into CSV for Tasker-based Health Connect import.
claims.evidence: The MIT project documents the export folder, weight/body-fat fields, CSV output and TaskerHealthConnect insertion workflow.

claims.claim: Huawei Health for iOS documents writing weight and motion/exercise data to HealthKit and obtaining exercise data from HealthKit.
claims.evidence: Huawei's current App Store description explicitly names weight synchronization, Huawei Health exercise data written to HealthKit and exercise data obtained from HealthKit.

claims.claim: Health Sync is an independent Android bridge and does not establish a native Huawei Health connector to Health Connect, Samsung Health or Google Fit.
claims.evidence: Health Sync documents its own synchronization and file-generation behavior as a third-party application.

claims.claim: Health Connect requires Android 9 or later and Google Play services, so many Huawei phones may require a separate Google-enabled Android environment for a bridge.
claims.evidence: Google's availability page explicitly requires Android 9 (API 28) or higher with Google Play services installed.

claims.claim: Any Huawei Health bridge to Google Fit is transition-sensitive because Google deprecated the Fit APIs in favor of Health Connect.
claims.evidence: Google's developer documentation directs migrations away from the deprecated Google Fit APIs.

claims.claim: Gadgetbridge can communicate locally with supported Huawei or Honor wearables without a vendor account, but it is not a Huawei Health cloud-history exporter.
claims.evidence: The project describes account-free Bluetooth gadget management and model-specific supported devices.

claims.claim: Huawei-TCX-Converter is an archived MIT project for converting legacy Huawei HiTrack workout files to TCX.
claims.evidence: The repository metadata reports an archived Python project, MIT license and a HiTrack-to-TCX purpose.

claims.claim: kobackupdec decrypts compatible user-password-protected Huawei backups but does not parse Huawei Health record semantics.
claims.evidence: The project documents HiSuite/KoBackup decryption and restored raw application/database paths, and explicitly declares end-of-life.

claims.claim: Current evidence does not establish that mainland-China and international Huawei accounts receive identical Huawei Health export workflows, formats or data.
claims.evidence: Huawei provides regional privacy information, but no comparative Huawei Health export specification was found.
